facts.text: HP³ Heat Flow Probe ('The Mole') was deployed at Elysium Planitia during InSight in 2018.

Germany's DLR Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package featured a 40-centimetre self-hammering tungsten penetrator designed to burrow 5 metres underground, trailing an instrumented cable with 14 temperature sensors to measure geothermal heat escape.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Discovered that the Martian regolith in Elysium has unexpected cohesive properties, forming a cement-like duricrust that challenged hammering mechanisms.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Elysium Planitia.
After months of innovative robotic teamwork with the IDA scoop pushing the mole, the instrument fully characterized the thermal conductivity of the upper 40 cm of soil.
